title: Finite local systems after forgetting cyclic module coefficients
statement: Let $Y$ be any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $n\geq1$ and $M$ a sheaf valued in modules over $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z/n)$ on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $G$ be its underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then $G$ is locally constant as an abelian sheaf [def-constructible-locally-constant] with finite stalks at every algebraically closed geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] if and only if there is an etale trivializing cover for $M$ with finite constant module values [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The conclusion concerns a single scheme, not a stratification; it asserts no module lift or uniqueness for arbitrary abelian sheaves.

proof.text: For a module constant-value trivialization on an etale object U, apply sheafCompose and constantCommuteCompose to obtain an abelian trivialization with the same underlying value. The pointwise restriction and forgetting commute definitionally.

Transport an abelian constant-value trivialization from the slice site over U to the small etale site of U.left, using overSheafEquivFunctorObjOverIso and constantSheafSheafCongrIso. Apply the pullback-stalk isomorphism and the constant-sheaf stalk isomorphism; their composite identifies the original abelian stalk at s composed with U.hom with the constant abelian value.

Suppose the underlying abelian sheaf is locally constant with finite algebraically closed geometric stalks. Take its trivializing cover and retain only members with a point; this remains jointly surjective since every covered point lies in a nonempty member. Apply cyclic-module reflection of constancy to each restriction to construct a module LocallyConstantDatum. Choose its constant module value E. Choose a point x on that member and the algebraic closure of its residue field, defining s:Spec Omega to U.left via SpecToEquivOfField. The stalk identification in step 2, after step 1, transfers the assumed finite abelian stalk to E. This gives the finite module values required on the right.

Conversely, forget the given finite module trivializations using step 1; they supply an abelian LocallyConstantDatum. For a geometric point s of Y, choose a member over its underlying point and lift s with exists_fac_of_etale_of_isSepClosed. Step 2 identifies its stalk with the finite underlying constant module value, so its stalk is finite. Combine the resulting local constancy and stalk finiteness. Empty schemes require no chosen cover member; n=1 is included in the cyclic reflection argument.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_local_cyclic_module_forget_iff {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (M : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)))) :
    let G := (sheafCompose Y.smallEtaleTopology
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj M
    (IsLocallyConstantSheaf G ∧
      ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y),
        Finite (((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj G)) ↔
    ∃ d : LocallyConstantDatum M, ∀ i : d.cover.I₀,
      ∃ A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)), Finite A ∧
        Nonempty ((M.over (d.cover.etalePrecoverageToEtale i)) ≅
          (constantSheaf (Y.smallEtaleTopology.over (d.cover.etalePrecoverageToEtale i))
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)))).obj A)
